questions.0.explain.t: The pipeline is the only mandatory path from code to production: putting checks there makes them automatic and repeatable.

questions.0.options.0.t: Because the pipeline is slow and the security checks need more stages

questions.0.options.1.t: Because every commit goes through it, so the control always runs, and early

questions.0.options.2.t: Because auditors require the pipeline logs for every release

questions.0.options.3.t: Because security tools only work inside a CI environment

questions.0.q.t: Why does security go inside the CI/CD pipeline, and not only at the end?

questions.1.explain.t: The gate turns a policy (no new criticals, no secrets) into an automatic pass or fail decision.

questions.1.options.0.t: A dashboard with the test coverage metrics of each repository

questions.1.options.1.t: A rule that blocks the pipeline from advancing if a criterion is not met

questions.1.options.2.t: A type of load test that measures the application's limit

questions.1.options.3.t: A manual code review done by the team at the end of the sprint

questions.2.explain.t: The pipeline holds credentials and publishes artifacts; compromising it means compromising everything it delivers.

questions.2.options.0.t: The pipeline running too many tests and delaying the delivery of changes

questions.2.options.1.t: Runners and tokens with excessive privilege being compromised

questions.2.options.2.t: The build taking more than a minute and blocking the deploy queue

questions.2.options.3.t: Using YAML instead of JSON in the configuration files

questions.2.q.t: What is a classic risk of the CI/CD pipeline itself?
